rationale: This role owns Roland DGA's product portfolio strategy, media recommendations, and customer success outcomes. Given Roland's TrueVIS printers are certified for 3-4 years outdoor durability, Tedlar represents a strategic opportunity to extend their value proposition to 12-20+ years—a 3-5x improvement that would dramatically differentiate Roland's solutions in the competitive wide-format printer market. This executive would care deeply about: (1) Enhancing Roland's 3M MCS and Avery Dennison ICS warranty certifications by pairing printers with premium overlaminates, (2) Reducing customer complaints about premature fading, cracking, or UV damage on vehicle wraps and outdoor signage, which directly impacts Roland's brand reputation and customer retention, (3) Creating bundled solutions (printer + ink + Tedlar overlaminate) that command premium pricing and improve gross margins, and (4) Competitive differentiation against Mimaki, HP Latex, and Epson in the outdoor graphics segment. Their KPIs around customer lifetime value, product differentiation, and market share growth make them the primary strategic decision-maker for materials partnerships.

This role leads Roland DGA's sales organization that sells directly to sign manufacturers, vehicle wrap shops, large-format print companies, and architectural graphics producers—the exact end-users of Tedlar films. Given Roland's active presence at PRINTING United, ISA Sign Expo, and Impressions Expo with live vehicle wrap demonstrations, the Director of Sales would immediately recognize Tedlar as a powerful sales enablement tool. They would care about: (1) Arming sales reps with a compelling TCO story—customers who buy Roland printers + Tedlar overlaminates achieve 12-20 year graphic lifespans vs. 3-4 years with standard laminates, drastically reducing replacement costs and maintenance, (2) Converting price-sensitive prospects to premium buyers by demonstrating superior long-term value and ROI, (3) Reducing warranty claims and customer service escalations related to outdoor durability failures, which consume sales team time and erode customer trust, and (4) Cross-selling and upselling opportunities within Roland's existing customer base of 150+ employees serving North and South America. Their revenue targets, customer acquisition costs, and win-rate metrics would directly benefit from a Tedlar partnership that strengthens Roland's competitive positioning in outdoor durable graphics.

This role owns Roland DGA's market positioning, customer education, and go-to-market messaging—critical for introducing Tedlar as part of Roland's recommended media stack. Given Roland's substantial trade show presence (PRINTING United 2024/2025, ISA 2024, Impressions 2026) and live vehicle wrap demonstrations, the marketing team actively shapes customer perceptions about durability and quality. They would care about: (1) Elevating Roland's brand positioning from '3-4 years outdoor durability' to '12-20+ years with Tedlar protection'—a transformative marketing message that repositions Roland as the premium choice for long-term outdoor applications, (2) Creating co-marketing content, case studies, and ROI calculators that demonstrate Tedlar's graffiti resistance, UV protection, and TCO benefits to Roland's target buyers (sign shops, wrap installers, architectural graphics companies), (3) Differentiating Roland's TrueVIS and VersaCAMM product lines in crowded trade show environments where competitors like Mimaki and HP Latex compete on similar specs, and (4) Supporting customer retention and referral programs by delivering measurably superior long-term results that generate testimonials and reduce churn. Their KPIs around brand awareness, lead generation quality, and customer satisfaction scores would improve significantly with Tedlar as a documented performance advantage in marketing campaigns and product launch materials for new printer series.
